pathway.title: CARVANA CO. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: - Leverage is low and falling because earnings grew, not because debt was repaid. Debt over Adjusted EBITDA fell from 4.09x at FY2024 to 2.29x at FY2025 and 1.90x on the last twelve months, while carrying debt moved only from USD 5,632 million to USD 5,115 million and USD 5,228 million. Adjusted EBITDA cover of cash interest is 5.88x, down from 11.98x at FY2024 because interest moved from payment in kind to cash. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_cvna-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 100–101; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C01

- Liquidity is strong today but rests on secured funding capacity that renews in 2027. Unrestricted cash is USD 3,049 million, equal to 58.3% of debt, against USD 71 million drawn on short-term facilities. The eight facilities total USD 5,600 million and 58.9% of that capacity matures by 2027-06-30, so the risk is lost capacity rather than a repayment, while 97.3% of corporate debt is due in 2031 or later. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 21–24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 78; calculation C07; calculation C08

- Earnings quality hinges on loan-sale gains, and the gain per dollar sold has already fallen. Gains were USD 381 million in Q3 2026, 64.1% of other sales and revenues, and the gain per dollar of receivables sold fell from about 10.0% to about 7.4% in a year, a shortfall of about USD 136 million in the quarter. Each point of gain per dollar is worth USD 206 million a year, 7.5% of Adjusted EBITDA. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18–19; calculation C02; calculation C03

- Unit economics are thinning while volume grows. Total gross profit per retail unit fell by USD 365 to USD 6,997 in Q3 2026 and the Adjusted EBITDA margin was 10.0% against 11.3%, so at the Q3 run rate that unit decline costs about USD 317 million a year, 11.5% of Adjusted EBITDA. Management attributes about USD 200 per unit of the pressure to fuel prices and rising benchmark rates. Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex99_1q32026.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex99_1q32026.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 70; calculation C04

- Stress arithmetic points to funding access, not earnings, as the break point. A fall of two percentage points in gain per dollar and a 10% fall in vehicle gross profit leave Adjusted EBITDA at USD 2,028 million, leverage at 2.58x and cash interest cover at 4.33x, but cash plus unused receivable lines cover only 4.2 months of loan production at the Q3 pace if every loan channel closed. Basis: calculation C05; calculation C06; calculation C09

- The debt structure is long-dated and first-lien, and the August 2026 refinancing is hedged only to July 2028. The Term Loan B of USD 1,660 million is due in 2033 and ranks pari passu with the 2031 secured notes; an interest rate swap fixes its base rate until 2028-07-31, so the all-in cash cost is about 6.3% and the cash saving against the 9% notes is USD 45 million a year while the swap runs, and each percentage point of Term SOFR is worth USD 17 million a year afterwards. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 25–27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 85; calculation C10

- Control and related-party features keep sponsor and governance risk at Medium. The Garcia Parties hold about 83% of the voting power, revenue from related parties is 21.9% of other sales and revenues, and the tax receivable agreement stands at USD 2,230 million with USD 100 million expected within twelve months against USD 37 million paid in the nine months to 2026-09-30. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_cvna-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 55; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 41–42; calculation C11; calculation C12

- Free cash flow is positive but converts only part of earnings because growth is funded through inventory and loans. Operating cash flow less capex was USD 889 million in FY2025 and USD 1,113 million over the last twelve months, 40.4% of Adjusted EBITDA, after USD 1,025 million of inventory growth in the nine months to 2026-09-30. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_cvna-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 103; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation C13

runs.text: Scale and growth are the first strength: retail units grew 39.4% in Q3 2026 while the industry was about flat, and Adjusted EBITDA reached USD 2,752 million over the last twelve months, which supports debt service and lets the company spend on capacity from earnings. Low leverage and large cash are the second: debt is 1.90x Adjusted EBITDA and unrestricted cash is USD 3,049 million, so earnings would have to fall far before debt service is threatened. Long-dated first-lien debt is the third: 97.3% of corporate debt falls due in 2031 or later and the Term Loan B ranks pari passu with the 2031 secured notes, so apart from USD 107 million of unsecured notes there is no corporate maturity wall before 2031. Liquidity is the fourth: USD 2,071 million of availability and USD 4,100 million of unused receivable lines against USD 71 million drawn. A supportive record on payouts is the fifth: no dividend and USD 126 million of sponsor equity in 2023. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18–29; 10-K_2025-12-31_cvna-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-K_2025-12-31_cvna-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 129; calculation C01; calculation C07; calculation C08; calculation C14; calculation C18

Dependence on loan-sale gains is the first weakness: 64.1% of other sales and revenues and 39.4% of nine-month gross profit, with the gain per dollar sold down from about 10.0% to about 7.4% in a year, so wider spreads reduce profit directly and cut the cash that funds growth. Thinning unit profit is the second: gross profit per retail unit fell USD 365 in Q3 2026 and the Adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 10.0% from 11.3%. Funding renewals are the third: 58.9% of the USD 5,600 million of short-term commitments matures by 2027-06-30 and Ally's commitment ends on 2027-07-26. Control and related-party features are the fourth: about 83% of votes with the Garcia Parties and 21.9% of other sales and revenues from DriveTime-related contracts. Claims outside debt are the fifth: a tax receivable agreement of USD 2,230 million that accelerates on a change of control and USD 300 million of trade floor plan payables outside debt. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18–24; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex99_1q32026.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C02; calculation C03; calculation C04; calculation C07; calculation C11; calculation C12; calculation C18

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The main new debt issue is the Term Loan B of USD 1.66 billion, entered on 2026-08-14 and fully drawn at closing at an issue price of 99.75%. It matures on 2033-08-14, amortises by USD 4 million a quarter from the March 2027 quarter, bears interest at Term SOFR plus 2.25% and ranks pari passu with the Senior Secured Notes on a first-priority lien over substantially all assets. It has no financial maintenance covenants, and a 1.00% premium applies to repricing prepayments until 2027-02-14. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 26–27

The loan proceeds and cash on hand redeemed the 2030 Senior Secured Notes of USD 1,660 million for USD 1,711 million, including a USD 50 million premium and USD 1 million of accrued interest, and Q3 2026 carries a loss on debt extinguishment of USD 53 million. The 2031 Senior Secured Notes of USD 2,269 million remain as the other first-priority instrument, and the refinancing replaced a 9% cash coupon with a loan whose effective rate is about 6.1%. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 24–27; calculation C12

Other financing events were smaller. A transportation fleet loan agreement of up to USD 250 million, signed on 2025-10-20, had USD 142 million outstanding at 2026-09-30 against USD 23 million at 2025-12-31. Ally raised its commitment to buy finance receivables to USD 8.0 billion on 2026-07-27, one fixed-pool agreement was increased by USD 500 million in Q3 2026, and one USD 600 million finance receivable facility was extended to October 2027 after the Q3 balance-sheet date. Two franchise dealerships were bought in 2026 for USD 40 million after five in 2025 for USD 160 million, and the Trade Floor Plan Facility that finances their new-vehicle inventory is now USD 300 million. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18–19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 29–30; 10-K_2025-12-31_cvna-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 84–85

No sale under the at-the-market program took place in 2026. The five-for-one stock split effected on 2026-05-08 gave each holder four additional shares per share held, so it changed share counts but not ownership proportions. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_cvna-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32

fields.value: - Minor: The 2026 proxy statement is not supplied. fields.value: - Minor: Executed debt and financing documents are not supplied, and the run settings declare none. The annual report's exhibit index lists the note indentures, the third-quarter report lists the August 2026 credit agreement as incorporated from a current report, and the floor plan and finance receivable facility agreements are likewise not supplied. Debt terms, guarantees, liens and covenants therefore rest on the filings' note summaries, and Legal & covenants, Covenant capacity, Structural priority, Intercreditor control, Recovery & fulcrum and Security selection cannot be completed from these sources.

Share data sit on two bases because a five-for-one split applies in the second- and third-quarter reports and letters but not in the annual report or the first-quarter report and letter, so share counts and per-share figures need conversion before comparison.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial foundation for CARVANA CO. as of 2026-11-05 under the credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the FY2023 to FY2025 annual statements, the Q1 to Q3 2026 interim statements, carrying-value debt, liquidity and events after the latest balance-sheet date, taken from the annual report and the three quarterly reports.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No external source was used. The shareholder letters are inventoried only.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage is moderate but earnings-dependent: total debt of USD 5,228 million is 1.96x last-twelve-months reported EBITDA and 1.90x Adjusted EBITDA, an improvement that came from earnings growth, not repayment.

fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 77; calculation C05; calculation C06

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net debt is USD 2,179 million after USD 3,049 million of unrestricted cash. Usable liquidity is narrower than USD 5,529 million of undrawn commitments suggests, because borrowing-base availability is USD 2,071 million and, after an October 2026 extension, every short-term facility matures in 2027; USD 300 million of trade floor plan payables sit outside debt, and no maturity ladder after the August 2026 refinancing is printed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The ladder is the annual report position at 2025-12-31 and predates the August 2026 refinancing, so its 2030 row still holds notes that were redeemed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The EBITDA column is the issuer Adjusted EBITDA, whereas the leverage and cover charts use reported EBITDA derived from operating income and depreciation and amortization.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Only the two pari passu secured instruments with a stated rank are shown, so this is not a complete capital structure or a recovery waterfall.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The bridge reconciles arithmetically but does not establish that any add-back is recurring or cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Gross leverage on reported EBITDA fell from 4.35x at FY2024 to 2.37x at FY2025 and 1.96x on the last twelve months to 2026-09-30, and the issuer-adjusted measure shows the same path, from 4.09x to 2.29x to 1.90x. Debt did not fall: carrying debt was USD 5,632 million, USD 5,115 million and USD 5,228 million, so the improvement came from Adjusted EBITDA rising from USD 1,378 million to USD 2,237 million and USD 2,752 million on the last twelve months. Because debt edged up after FY2025 and the August 2026 refinancing left gross principal unchanged, creditors' protection depends on EBITDA holding at this level.

fields.value: The strongest contrary evidence is cash: unrestricted cash rose from USD 1,716 million to USD 2,327 million and USD 3,049 million, so net leverage on reported EBITDA is 3.02x, 1.29x and 0.82x. That view wins only while the cash stays on the balance sheet; working capital can reabsorb it, as inventory growth did with USD 1,025 million in the nine months to 2026-09-30.

fields.value: Of USD 5,161 million of principal, USD 4,036 million is corporate debt, made up of the 2031 secured notes of USD 2,269 million, the Term Loan B of USD 1,660 million and unsecured notes of USD 107 million, and USD 1,125 million is asset-based funding tied to specific collateral; finance leases of USD 100 million are carried inside debt as well. Floor plan and securitization financing of USD 498 million is matched to inventory and retained interests, so it should not be read as industrial leverage, while the secured notes and Term Loan B of USD 3,929 million rank equally and equal 1.47x reported and 1.43x adjusted EBITDA.

fields.value: The August 2026 refinancing replaced USD 1,660 million of 2030 secured notes with a Term Loan B of the same amount due 2033-08-14, at a cost of USD 50 million of redemption premium and a USD 53 million loss on extinguishment, and left gross principal unchanged. The only printed maturity ladder is at 2025-12-31 and still shows USD 1,708 million due in 2030, so it overstates the 2030 wall and omits the Term Loan B; creditors should read the ladder chart as the position before the refinancing.

fields.value: Cash interest paid was USD 115 million in FY2024, USD 336 million in FY2025 and USD 468 million over the last twelve months, against accrued interest expense, net of USD 651 million, USD 505 million and USD 396 million; the difference is interest paid in kind, USD 458 million in FY2024 and USD 182 million in FY2025, and the 2026 cash flow prints none. Reported EBITDA therefore covers cash interest 11.26x, 6.42x and 5.71x: cover falls although EBITDA grows because interest moved from payment in kind to cash, so the FY2024 ratio overstates debt service capacity.

fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cvna-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 101, 103, 166; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 6, 54; calculation C06; calculation C14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Operating cash flow was USD 1,036 million in FY2025 and USD 900 million in the nine months to 2026-09-30, after inventory growth of USD 734 million and USD 1,025 million, and with capex of USD 147 million and USD 166 million free cash flow was USD 889 million and USD 734 million. Operating cash flow also carries finance receivable originations of USD 14,187 million in nine months 2026 against USD 14,722 million of sale proceeds, so cash generation depends on continued loan sales as well as on vehicle margins.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash of USD 3,049 million is unrestricted, and restricted cash of USD 123 million is separate. Undrawn commitments of USD 5,529 million overstate usable liquidity: the issuer's availability measure, which limits borrowing to pledgeable inventory and finance receivables, is USD 2,071 million, and the seven finance receivable lines fund receivables only through special-purpose subsidiaries. After an October 2026 extension of one line, all eight short-term facilities mature in 2027, the first on 2027-02-14, so renewal is a nearer funding test than the 2031 notes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 22–24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 78; calculation C07; calculation C17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Two claims sit outside debt. Trade floor plan payables of USD 300 million, up from USD 64 million at 2025-12-31, are interest-bearing inventory financing secured by the financed vehicles but are carried in accounts payable, which rose from USD 1,100 million to USD 1,574 million; adding them lifts leverage on Adjusted EBITDA to 2.01x. The tax receivable agreement liability is USD 2,130 million, and USD 37 million was paid in the nine months to 2026-09-30, so it is a recorded obligation outside debt that reduces cash available to creditors.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reported EBITDA is derived because the issuer states only Adjusted EBITDA. The operating basis is used because a net-income basis would give negative USD 110 million for FY2025 and USD 407 million for the last twelve months, depressed by USD 2,200 million of tax receivable agreement expense, and would put leverage at 12.85x. Adjusted EBITDA exceeds reported EBITDA by only USD 82 million over the last twelve months, which is share-based compensation of USD 97 million in SG&A and USD 4 million in cost of sales and other operating expense of USD 2 million, less warrant revenue of USD 21 million, so the add-backs are small and mostly non-cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cvna-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 78, 80, 103; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 77; calculation C11; calculation C18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The only event after the balance-sheet date is the October 2026 extension of one finance receivable facility from 2026-10-09 to 2027-10-15; it changes neither debt nor cash and is excluded from the period figures. The quarterly report has no subsequent-events note, so no further event is established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Each row restates its inputs; amounts are USD millions as printed and results are exact at source precision unless a ratio is stated to two or four decimals.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Medium: No principal maturity schedule is printed at 2026-09-30. The only ladder is the annual report's at 2025-12-31, which precedes the August 2026 refinancing and still shows USD 1,708 million due in 2030, and the real estate financing, securitization financing and fleet financing have no dated schedule, so a current maturity wall cannot be drawn without estimating. A schedule at 2026-09-30 would close this.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Medium: Trade floor plan payables of USD 300 million sit in accounts payable and accrued liabilities, outside Total Debt, although the facility is interest-bearing and secured by financed inventory and the payables equal the USD 300 million line. Debt is shown as the issuer classifies it, and the sensitivity is in the calculations; whether lenders treat the payables as debt is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Medium: Financial maintenance covenants for the Floor Plan Facility and the finance receivable facilities are not disclosed; the issuer states only that it was in compliance with all debt covenants at 2026-09-30, and the Term Loan B credit agreement has no financial maintenance covenants. Covenant headroom is not established and no capacity is inferred.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Medium: The legal rank of the floor plan, the finance receivable facilities, the securitization financing, the real estate financing, the fleet financing, the finance leases and the USD 107 million of unsecured notes against the secured notes and the Term Loan B is not stated, so the debt stack shows only the two pari passu secured instruments and cannot support a priority or recovery view. Executed documents would close this.

fields.value: - Low: The company reports one operating segment, so no segment revenue schedule exists and no segment sum is stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Low: Source dashes stay missing, not zero, in the statement tables, for example other operating expense and loss on debt extinguishment in Q1 and Q2 2026, payment-in-kind interest in nine months 2026 and goodwill at FY2024. Reported totals remain usable; the Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation check reads a dash add-back as no amount for that check only.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Low: Cash taxes paid are printed only for the nine-month periods, not for the fiscal years, so cash tax cover is not calculable for FY2023 to FY2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Low: Capital expenditure is not split between maintenance and growth, and the FY2024 undrawn commitments are printed only as USD 4.1 billion, rounded.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Low: Stand-alone fourth quarters and discrete Q1 and Q2 2025 columns are not tabulated; the last-twelve-months figures are built from the full year and the nine-month periods, which is the basis the issuer reports.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Low: Issuance costs on revolving facilities are carried in other assets, not in the debt lines, so carrying debt for those lines is gross of those costs.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business, ownership and transaction fact pack for CARVANA CO. as of 2026-11-05 under the credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the business and operating model, ownership and control, related-party arrangements, financing transactions and the sponsor and governance behaviour evidenced in the FY2025 annual report and the three 2026 quarterly reports, with the three shareholder letters read for management statements.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No external source was used. The proxy statement, indentures, credit agreements and subsidiary list are not in the supplied sources.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Carvana's creditors are exposed to loan-sale market access and to related-party contracts as much as to vehicle demand, so funding access and control terms matter more than growth. Gains on loan sales supplied 64.1% of other sales and revenues in Q3 2026, and revenue from related parties supplied 21.9% of them in the nine months to September 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18–19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 70; calculation C05; calculation C07

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The online used-car retailer is controlled by the Garcia Parties, Ernest Garcia II, Ernest Garcia III and their entities, who held about 83% of the voting power at the 2025 year-end, and a tax receivable agreement liability of USD 2.2 billion, USD 1.7 billion of it owed to related parties, accelerates on a change of control. Sponsor and governance risk is Medium: no dividend or debt-funded distribution is documented and the Garcia Parties committed up to USD 126 million of equity in 2023, but control, related-party dependence and missing ownership detail keep it above Low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Loan-sale funding is the dependency that matters most. Gains on loan sales were USD 381 million in Q3 2026, 64.1% of other sales and revenues, which carry a 100% gross margin, and other sales and revenues were 39.4% of gross profit in the nine months to September 2026. Pricing depends on investor demand and credit spreads, so wider spreads would cut gross profit directly. The gain earned per dollar of receivables sold fell from about 10.0% to about 7.4% over the year. Committed capacity is large but finite: the unused commitment of Ally, its committed forward-flow buyer, lasts 9.0 months at the Q3 pace against 9.8 months of remaining term, and USD 8.3 billion of fixed-pool capacity remains.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18–19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 60; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 70; 10-K_2025-12-31_cvna-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 43–44; calculation C04; calculation C07; calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Control rests with one controlling group, and the contracts route services and cash to it. The Garcia Parties hold ten votes per Class B share while their as-exchanged Class A ownership stays at or above 25%, can elect every director and own substantially all of DriveTime. The charter waives their duty to avoid competing businesses. Controlled-company exemptions from board independence rules are available but not used, and holders of LLC units other than Carvana Co. own 34.9% of the operating group.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The tax receivable agreement is a debt-like claim that competes for cash and accelerates on a change of control. The liability was USD 2,228 million at 2025-12-31, equal to 43.6% of balance-sheet debt at that date, and USD 1,721 million of it was due to related parties. Payments of USD 37 million in the nine months to September 2026 were small, but a merger, breach or early termination makes the obligation immediately payable, and the Senior Secured Notes also carry a change-of-control offer at 101%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - DriveTime is an embedded related-party provider, and the dependence is rising. Vehicle service contract commissions on contracts administered by DriveTime were USD 349 million in the nine months to September 2026, and revenue from related parties rose from 17.4% of other sales and revenues in FY2024 to 20.0% in FY2025 and 21.9% in the nine months, when it equalled 8.6% of gross profit. DriveTime also administers the limited warranty, services receivables and leases reconditioning centres, and the annual report says these arrangements cannot be assumed to be arm's length.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cvna-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-K_2025-12-31_cvna-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 124–127; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14–17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 70; calculation C05; calculation C06; calculation C08

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The operating model scales with retail units, but unit economics are thinning at the margin. Retail units grew 39.4% in Q3 2026 and retail vehicles reached 75.4% of revenue in the nine months to September 2026 against 71.5% in FY2025, while total gross profit per unit fell by USD 365 to USD 6,997 as loan sale spreads and wholesale profit per unit declined. Management attributes about USD 200 per unit of pressure to fuel prices and rising benchmark rates, and the Q3 run rate uses 58.0% of the retail production capacity management states.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex99_1q32026.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex99_1q32026.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 70; calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The August 2026 refinancing cut cost and extended maturity without weakening ranking, but it moved fixed-rate debt to a floating rate. The Term Loan B of USD 1.66 billion is due in 2033, ranks pari passu on first-priority liens and has no financial maintenance covenants. Its effective rate of about 6.1% compares with a 9% cash coupon on the redeemed notes, an indicative saving of USD 48 million a year at the current benchmark, which the management letter says has been rising rapidly.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Capital allocation and sponsor conduct have favoured growth, debt reduction and support over payouts. No dividend was paid in FY2025 and no issuer purchase of equity was reported for the fourth quarter. The Garcia Parties committed up to USD 126 million of equity in 2023 and bought units that part-funded a tender offer for the 2025 unsecured notes, USD 539 million of equity was raised in Q3 2025 with no at-the-market sales in 2026, and USD 611 million of 2028 secured notes were repurchased or redeemed in 2025. Acquisitions were small: USD 160 million for five dealerships in 2025 and USD 40 million for two in 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a Medium level is the documented record. No dividend or debt-funded distribution appears in the sources, the Garcia Parties committed up to USD 126 million of equity in 2023, USD 539 million of public equity was raised in Q3 2025, the 2028 secured notes were redeemed early and the August 2026 loan ranks pari passu with no maintenance covenant. Related-party revenue was 8.6% of gross profit in the nine months to September 2026 and related-party payables are only USD 35 million. Loan-sale capacity is committed with four counterparties, Ally for up to USD 8.0 billion and three fixed-pool purchasers for up to USD 12.5 billion in total, and management reports eight consecutive quarters of retail unit growth of about 40%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The level would fall to Low if the proxy statement showed a board with a majority of independent directors and arm's-length pricing for the DriveTime contracts, and if the indentures limited restricted payments and affiliate transactions tightly. It would rise to High on a distribution, a new unrestricted-subsidiary designation of a core asset, a shortening of the loan-sale commitments, gain on loan sales falling well below the Q3 2026 level, or a sell-down that took the Garcia Parties below the 25% ownership test for ten-vote shares.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The proxy statement for the 2026 annual meeting is not in the sources, so board independence, sponsor fees and the Garcia Parties' economic ownership are not established, and the Medium sponsor and governance level could move either way once they are known.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The indentures and credit agreements are not supplied, so the capacity to pay related parties, make distributions or designate unrestricted subsidiaries is not established; the assessment rests on documented behaviour, not on legal capacity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The terms of the September 2023 exchange offers are not described, so the record of creditor treatment in 2023 is incomplete and may understate creditor-adverse behaviour.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Loan-sale volumes are printed in rounded billions and the three sale channels are assumed to be additive, so the finding that gain per dollar sold has fallen is approximate and could be narrower or wider.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The control percentage is stated only at 2025-12-31, so a change in the Garcia Parties' voting power during 2026 is not established, although Class B share counts did not change.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main new debt issue is the Term Loan B of USD 1.66 billion, entered on 2026-08-14 and fully drawn at closing at an issue price of 99.75%. It matures on 2033-08-14, amortises by USD 4 million a quarter from the March 2027 quarter, bears interest at Term SOFR plus 2.25% and ranks pari passu with the Senior Secured Notes on a first-priority lien over substantially all assets. It has no financial maintenance covenants, and a 1.00% premium applies to repricing prepayments until 2027-02-14.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The loan proceeds and cash on hand redeemed the 2030 Senior Secured Notes of USD 1,660 million for USD 1,711 million, including a USD 50 million premium and USD 1 million of accrued interest, and Q3 2026 carries a loss on debt extinguishment of USD 53 million. The 2031 Senior Secured Notes of USD 2,269 million remain as the other first-priority instrument, and the refinancing replaced a 9% cash coupon with a loan whose effective rate is about 6.1%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Other financing events were smaller. A transportation fleet loan agreement of up to USD 250 million, signed on 2025-10-20, had USD 142 million outstanding at 2026-09-30 against USD 23 million at 2025-12-31. Ally raised its commitment to buy finance receivables to USD 8.0 billion on 2026-07-27, one fixed-pool agreement was increased by USD 500 million in Q3 2026, and one USD 600 million finance receivable facility was extended to October 2027 after the Q3 balance-sheet date. Two franchise dealerships were bought in 2026 for USD 40 million after five in 2025 for USD 160 million, and the Trade Floor Plan Facility that finances their new-vehicle inventory is now USD 300 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No sale under the at-the-market program took place in 2026. The five-for-one stock split effected on 2026-05-08 gave each holder four additional shares per share held, so it changed share counts but not ownership proportions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sponsor and governance risk level: Medium.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Each row restates its inputs; amounts are USD millions as printed unless a billion figure is stated, and results are rounded as shown.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Medium: The 2026 proxy statement is not in the sources, so the Garcia Parties' share of Class A stock and LLC units, board independence and any sponsor fees are not stated. The control percentage in the annual report is at 2025-12-31 only. Obtaining the proxy statement would settle the economic ownership and independence questions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Medium: The indentures, the Term Loan B credit agreement and the floor plan and receivable facility agreements are not supplied, so restricted payment, affiliate transaction and unrestricted subsidiary capacity are not established and no capacity is inferred from behaviour.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Medium: The commission rates, pricing and termination rights of the DriveTime contracts are not stated, so whether revenue of this size from a related party is at market terms is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Low: The terms and participation of the September 2023 exchange offers are not described in the supplied documents, and the FY2023 gain on debt extinguishment is the only trace of them.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Low: The three fixed-pool purchasers are unnamed, so counterparty concentration in loan sales beyond Ally cannot be assessed.

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit synthesis for CARVANA CO. as of 2026-11-05 under the credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the business, ownership, financial profile, outlook, downside scenario and monitoring view built from the FY2025 annual report, the three 2026 quarterly reports and the three shareholder letters, with the supplied Source readiness, Financial foundation and Business & governance analyses.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No external source was used. Credit ratings, market prices and loan performance data are not in the supplied sources.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit quality is adequate and improving: low leverage and cash balances protect creditors, but earnings depend on loan-sale markets and funding lines that renew during 2027, so a funding shock rather than an earnings fall is the main path to deterioration. Total debt of USD 5,228 million is 1.90x last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA and net debt is 0.79x, and two illustrative shocks to loan-sale gains and vehicle profit lift leverage only to 2.58x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C01; calculation C06

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The weakest dimension is diversification, because other sales and revenues, which are all gross profit, were 39.4% of nine-month gross profit and depend on investors buying the loans Carvana originates. Sponsor and governance risk is Medium, and the tax receivable agreement, related-party revenue and the 2028 expiry of the rate hedge are the secondary risks.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 60; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 70; calculation C02

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Leverage is low and falling because earnings grew, not because debt was repaid. Debt over Adjusted EBITDA fell from 4.09x at FY2024 to 2.29x at FY2025 and 1.90x on the last twelve months, while carrying debt moved only from USD 5,632 million to USD 5,115 million and USD 5,228 million. Adjusted EBITDA cover of cash interest is 5.88x, down from 11.98x at FY2024 because interest moved from payment in kind to cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_cvna-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 100–101; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C01

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Liquidity is strong today but rests on secured funding capacity that renews in 2027. Unrestricted cash is USD 3,049 million, equal to 58.3% of debt, against USD 71 million drawn on short-term facilities. The eight facilities total USD 5,600 million and 58.9% of that capacity matures by 2027-06-30, so the risk is lost capacity rather than a repayment, while 97.3% of corporate debt is due in 2031 or later.

fields.value: - Earnings quality hinges on loan-sale gains, and the gain per dollar sold has already fallen. Gains were USD 381 million in Q3 2026, 64.1% of other sales and revenues, and the gain per dollar of receivables sold fell from about 10.0% to about 7.4% in a year, a shortfall of about USD 136 million in the quarter. Each point of gain per dollar is worth USD 206 million a year, 7.5% of Adjusted EBITDA.

fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18–19; calculation C02; calculation C03

fields.value: - Unit economics are thinning while volume grows. Total gross profit per retail unit fell by USD 365 to USD 6,997 in Q3 2026 and the Adjusted EBITDA margin was 10.0% against 11.3%, so at the Q3 run rate that unit decline costs about USD 317 million a year, 11.5% of Adjusted EBITDA. Management attributes about USD 200 per unit of the pressure to fuel prices and rising benchmark rates.

fields.value: - Stress arithmetic points to funding access, not earnings, as the break point. A fall of two percentage points in gain per dollar and a 10% fall in vehicle gross profit leave Adjusted EBITDA at USD 2,028 million, leverage at 2.58x and cash interest cover at 4.33x, but cash plus unused receivable lines cover only 4.2 months of loan production at the Q3 pace if every loan channel closed.

fields.value: - The debt structure is long-dated and first-lien, and the August 2026 refinancing is hedged only to July 2028. The Term Loan B of USD 1,660 million is due in 2033 and ranks pari passu with the 2031 secured notes; an interest rate swap fixes its base rate until 2028-07-31, so the all-in cash cost is about 6.3% and the cash saving against the 9% notes is USD 45 million a year while the swap runs, and each percentage point of Term SOFR is worth USD 17 million a year afterwards.

fields.value: - Control and related-party features keep sponsor and governance risk at Medium. The Garcia Parties hold about 83% of the voting power, revenue from related parties is 21.9% of other sales and revenues, and the tax receivable agreement stands at USD 2,230 million with USD 100 million expected within twelve months against USD 37 million paid in the nine months to 2026-09-30.

fields.value: - Free cash flow is positive but converts only part of earnings because growth is funded through inventory and loans. Operating cash flow less capex was USD 889 million in FY2025 and USD 1,113 million over the last twelve months, 40.4% of Adjusted EBITDA, after USD 1,025 million of inventory growth in the nine months to 2026-09-30.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against treating funding as the weak point is the record of renewal and growth. Ally's commitment to buy loans rose from USD 4.0 billion in January 2025 to USD 6.0 billion in October 2025 and USD 8.0 billion in July 2026, fixed-pool commitments reached USD 12.5 billion, seven receivable facilities are undrawn, USD 13.9 billion of loans were sold in the nine months to 2026-09-30, and the August 2026 refinancing priced a seven-year loan at a lower cost than the notes it replaced. On that record the funding channel has widened as volume grew, and the shock modelled here would need both a market closure and a fall in gains at once.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cvna-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 129; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18–19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 23–26; calculation C09; calculation C17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The assessment of market access would move from average to strong if the facilities due in 2027 were extended beyond 2027 and Ally's commitment were renewed three months ahead of its 2027-07-26 expiry, as the July 2026 amendment was, with gain per dollar sold holding at about 7.4% or better. It would move to weak if any loan-sale commitment were shortened, if the facility due 2027-02-14 were not extended, if gain per dollar fell below about 5.4%, or if gross profit per unit fell by another USD 365 to about USD 6,632, either of which would move the profile toward the modelled stress level.

fields.value: - Performance data on the loans Carvana sells, such as delinquency and loss rates, are not printed, so the strength of investor demand for its loans, the basis of the funding conclusion, cannot be tested directly.

fields.value: - The stress steps use assumed shocks and rounded loan-sale volumes, so the 2.58x leverage and 4.2 month runway are illustrations of sensitivity and not forecasts, and a different shock size would move the conclusion that earnings are not the break point.

fields.value: - Management will stop giving annual and quarterly outlooks from the Q4 2026 call and will move its targets to GAAP measures in 2027, so the outlook view rests on the last guidance, which has no stated range after 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - A maturity ladder after the August 2026 refinancing is not printed, so the maturity profile is built from instrument maturities and could differ for amortizing asset-based balances.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Scale and growth are the first strength: retail units grew 39.4% in Q3 2026 while the industry was about flat, and Adjusted EBITDA reached USD 2,752 million over the last twelve months, which supports debt service and lets the company spend on capacity from earnings. Low leverage and large cash are the second: debt is 1.90x Adjusted EBITDA and unrestricted cash is USD 3,049 million, so earnings would have to fall far before debt service is threatened. Long-dated first-lien debt is the third: 97.3% of corporate debt falls due in 2031 or later and the Term Loan B ranks pari passu with the 2031 secured notes, so apart from USD 107 million of unsecured notes there is no corporate maturity wall before 2031. Liquidity is the fourth: USD 2,071 million of availability and USD 4,100 million of unused receivable lines against USD 71 million drawn. A supportive record on payouts is the fifth: no dividend and USD 126 million of sponsor equity in 2023.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18–29; 10-K_2025-12-31_cvna-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-K_2025-12-31_cvna-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 129; calculation C01; calculation C07; calculation C08; calculation C14; calculation C18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Dependence on loan-sale gains is the first weakness: 64.1% of other sales and revenues and 39.4% of nine-month gross profit, with the gain per dollar sold down from about 10.0% to about 7.4% in a year, so wider spreads reduce profit directly and cut the cash that funds growth. Thinning unit profit is the second: gross profit per retail unit fell USD 365 in Q3 2026 and the Adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 10.0% from 11.3%. Funding renewals are the third: 58.9% of the USD 5,600 million of short-term commitments matures by 2027-06-30 and Ally's commitment ends on 2027-07-26. Control and related-party features are the fourth: about 83% of votes with the Garcia Parties and 21.9% of other sales and revenues from DriveTime-related contracts. Claims outside debt are the fifth: a tax receivable agreement of USD 2,230 million that accelerates on a change of control and USD 300 million of trade floor plan payables outside debt.

fields.value: The tax receivable agreement liability is USD 2,230 million at 2026-09-30, made up of USD 2,130 million carried as a long-term liability and USD 100 million expected within twelve months in other current liabilities. Financial foundation quotes the USD 2,130 million long-term line and Business & governance quotes USD 2.2 billion at that date; the year-end total was USD 2,265 million, of which Business & governance quotes the USD 2,228 million long-term line. The totals used here are the roll-forward totals.

fields.value: Business & governance describes the Term Loan B as floating and puts the interest saving at USD 48 million a year using the 6.1% effective rate. The quarterly report shows an interest rate swap on USD 1,660 million that fixes the base rate until 2028-07-31, so the cash cost is about 6.3% to that date and the cash saving against the 9% notes is USD 45 million a year; Term SOFR exposure of USD 17 million per percentage point returns after the swap ends. Financial foundation does not mention the swap.

fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 25–27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 85; calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Carvana is an online used-car retailer that sources, reconditions, finances and delivers vehicles through its own network, and it earns profit from three lines. Retail vehicle sales were 75.4% of nine-month revenue but only 49.5% of gross profit, while other sales and revenues, which are loan-sale gains and commissions with no cost of sales, were 39.4% of gross profit. Cash flow therefore depends on retail volume and on investors buying the loans it originates, which makes visibility shorter than the revenue base suggests, and refinancing confidence rests on loan-sale access as much as on vehicle sales. Retail units grew 39.4% in Q3 2026 while the industry was about flat, according to management.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_cvna-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 4–6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 58–60; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 70; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex99_1q32026.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation C02; calculation C14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The Garcia Parties hold about 83% of the voting power through ten-vote Class B shares and own DriveTime, so control and a key counterparty sit with the same group. Carvana Co. owns about 65.1% of the operating group, and the holders of the other units have a tax receivable agreement claim of USD 2,230 million that accelerates on a change of control. Behaviour on record is creditor-supportive, including USD 126 million of equity committed in 2023 and no dividend in FY2025, but the legal capacity to change that is not established, so sponsor and governance risk is Medium.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_cvna-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 55; 10-K_2025-12-31_cvna-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 129; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 41–42; calculation C12; calculation C18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is volume-driven and discretionary. Retail vehicle sales rose 53.8% in Q3 2026 on 39.4% more units and a higher revenue per unit of USD 28,263 against USD 25,625, a mix of share gains and used-car price appreciation that can reverse. There is no contract revenue: every sale is a one-off transaction with a seven-day return right, and competitors include CarMax, Amazon and DriveTime, which holds a cross-license and could compete. The growth is therefore share gain in a flat industry and not visible recurring revenue, and higher interest rates raise monthly payments and weaken demand.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 70; 10-K_2025-12-31_cvna-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 26–28; calculation C14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins are defended by scale, not by contract. The Adjusted EBITDA margin was 10.0% in Q3 2026 against 11.3% a year earlier, so growth of 39.4% in units did not stop it falling by 1.3 percentage points. SG&A was USD 805 million in the quarter, of which advertising was USD 152 million and compensation USD 255 million, both linked to volume, while fixed and variable cost shares are not disclosed. Management attributes USD 365 of lower gross profit per unit to loan pricing given back to customers and lower wholesale profit, so margin holds under volume pressure only if loan-sale spreads hold.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex99_1q32026.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex99_1q32026.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 73; calculation C04; calculation C14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capex is light, at 0.7% of FY2025 revenue, but conversion is modest because growth is funded through inventory and loans. Operating cash flow less capex was USD 889 million in FY2025, USD 734 million in the nine months to 2026-09-30 and USD 1,113 million over the last twelve months, which is 40.4% of Adjusted EBITDA, after USD 1,025 million of inventory growth. Cash interest of USD 468 million is covered 5.88x, and free cash flow depends on loan sales continuing, because originations of USD 14,187 million in the nine months were met by sale proceeds of USD 14,722 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_cvna-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 103; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation C01; calculation C13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is intense but fragmented: the ten largest used-car retailers held less than 10% of the market in 2024 and Carvana has about 2% of it, so share gains can continue, while price competition from CarMax, Amazon and franchise dealers limits margin. New entrants face high operating complexity in reconditioning and logistics, though technology changes such as artificial intelligence and autonomous vehicles are cited as risks to the model. Buyer power is high because switching costs are low and returns are allowed for seven days. Supplier power matters most in funding: vehicles come from customers, auctions and fleets, but Ally and the loan buyers decide how much Carvana can sell, and commercial suppliers review their disposition channels through requests for proposals.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cvna-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2025-12-31_cvna-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 26–29; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex99_1q32026.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 62; calculation C18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Economic factors are a primary credit driver because benchmark rates and used-car prices set loan-sale pricing and affordability: management reports rapidly rising benchmark rates and fuel prices that cost about USD 200 per unit in Q3 2026. Regulators scrutinise advertising, financing and insurance in used-vehicle sales, which could narrow Carvana's differentiation, and the quarterly report says tariffs and the conflict involving Iran did not materially affect Q3 results. Technology and social factors are not quantified in the sources and are not treated as primary drivers.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex99_1q32026.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2025-12-31_cvna-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 61; calculation C04

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths are scale and growth, low leverage with large cash, and long-dated first-lien corporate debt, which together give creditors a margin of safety today. Weaknesses are dependence on loan-sale gains, thinning unit profit, and control and related-party features. The main opportunity is renewal of the 2027 facilities and Ally's commitment on longer terms, which would remove the nearest funding test and lift the profile. The main threats are wider loan-sale spreads, a fall in used-car prices that creates markdown risk on inventory, and a change of control that would accelerate the tax receivable agreement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18–19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 23–24; 10-K_2025-12-31_cvna-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-K_2025-12-31_cvna-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 49–50; calculation C01; calculation C08

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Scale and market position is strong: retail units grew 39.4% in Q3 2026 and the business has about 2% of the used market, which leaves large room for share gains but shows it is far from dominant. Competitive advantage is average: management says its margins are about twice the industry average, but switching costs are low and rivals can copy the online model. Business diversification is weak: a single market, the United States, one online channel and one product category, with other sales and revenues tied to retail units and to loan buyers. Cost and capex flexibility is average: capex is only 0.7% of revenue and advertising can be cut, but the fixed cost share is not disclosed. Margin stability is average: the Adjusted EBITDA margin was 3.1% in FY2023, 10.1% in FY2024, 11.0% in FY2025 and 10.0% in Q3 2026, a short record that has not met a downturn. Free cash flow stability is average: positive in each period but only 40.4% of Adjusted EBITDA. Ability to refinance and access capital markets is average: USD 1,660 million was refinanced in August 2026 and USD 13.9 billion of loans were sold in nine months, but all eight short-term facilities mature in 2027. Liquidity position is strong: USD 3,049 million of unrestricted cash and USD 2,071 million of issuer-defined availability against USD 71 million drawn. Financial policy and governance is average: supportive conduct with concentrated control.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex99_1q32026.htm.jsonl, pages 1–2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 78; calculation C01; calculation C07; calculation C09; calculation C13; calculation C14; calculation C15; calculation C18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main supports are liquidity and falling leverage; the constraints are diversification and funding dependence; the trend is improving on earnings but softening on unit profit; and the missing data are ratings, loan performance and a post-refinancing maturity ladder.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next 12 to 24 months management guides only to the end of 2026, with a sequential rise in Q4 retail units and Adjusted EBITDA at the higher end of USD 2.7 billion to USD 3.0 billion, against LTM Adjusted EBITDA of USD 2,752 million, and Q4 is seasonally the weakest quarter. Tailwinds are capacity already in place, with the Q3 run rate at 58.0% of stated capacity, and the option to reprice the Term Loan B without the 1.00% premium after 2027-02-14. Headwinds are the 2027 renewals, Ally's commitment ending on 2027-07-26, tax receivable payments rising to about USD 100 million over twelve months, and rising benchmark rates and fuel prices. Over three to five years management targets a retail unit volume 3.45 times the Q3 run rate at a 12.5% operating margin between 2030 and 2035, which needs more reconditioning capacity and is a management goal, not a forecast.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex99_1q32026.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex99_1q32026.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex99_1q32026.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 41; calculation C01; calculation C12; calculation C16; calculation C18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The initiating condition is a rise in benchmark rates and wider asset-backed spreads at a time of lower used-car prices, the conditions management already names. The first operational break is the price investors pay for loans: gain per dollar of receivables sold falls further, as it did by about 2.6 percentage points over the past year. The financial transmission is direct because other sales and revenues are all gross profit: two percentage points less gain on the Q3 pace removes USD 412 million a year, and a 10% fall in vehicle gross profit removes USD 312 million more, leaving Adjusted EBITDA at USD 2,028 million, leverage at 2.58x and cash interest cover at 4.33x. Liquidity then depends on whether loan buyers keep buying: if every channel closed, cash plus unused receivable lines would fund about 4.2 months of loan production, and the 2027 facility renewals would fall due in the same period. Management levers are slowing unit growth and inventory purchases, which release working capital, and cutting advertising. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid distress under the earnings shocks alone, and insufficient to absorb a prolonged closure of the loan-sale channel. The observable triggers are gain per dollar sold, the Ally renewal and the 2027 facility extensions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C03; calculation C05; calculation C06; calculation C09; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex99_1q32026.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18–19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cvna-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 23–24

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Carvana presents an adequate business profile supported by scale, growth, low leverage and large cash, but credit quality is constrained by dependence on loan-sale gains, thinning unit profit and concentrated control. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because free cash flow is positive but converts only 40.4% of Adjusted EBITDA. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the renewal of the 2027 facilities, Ally's commitment and the price investors pay for Carvana's loans. The primary downside path is a loan-sale funding shock that cuts gains and tightens liquidity at the same time. Further analysis would require ratings, loan performance data, the indentures and a maturity ladder after the August 2026 refinancing. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: loan-sale funding stress.
